name: Mediterranean Gull
rangeDescription: North sea to mediterranean and black sea; winters to northern africa
description: Medium-sized gull, slightly larger than Black-headed Gull, more similar to Common Gull in size and shape but bill stouter. Adult is distinctive, the only small gull with snow-white wingtips; breeding plumage has black hood.

name: Principe Sunbird
rangeDescription: Príncipe island (gulf of guinea)
description: A medium-sized dark sunbird with a graduated, white-tipped tail. Male has a blue-purple iridescent throat and upper tail; female and juvenile are dull yellow underneath.
imageCreditName: Lars Petersson | My World of Bird Photography

name: Western Wattled-Honeyeater
rangeDescription: Fiji (viti levu, ovalau, and islands in yasawa archipelago)
description: A medium-sized, mostly olive honeyeater with a slightly grayish cast to the throat, underside, and cheek. Note the dark blackish moustachial stripe with small bright yellow wattle, which are diagnostic, and the beady pale eye.
imageCreditName: Lars Petersson | My World of Bird Photography

name: Wood Warbler
rangeDescription: Breeds europe and russia; winters in tropical africa
description: Small warbler with subtly distinctive plumage: muted lime green above, silky white below, with a pale yellow throat and yellow eyebrows. Favors shady deciduous and mixed woods for breeding, especially areas with beech and oak.

name: Tanimbar Eclectus
rangeDescription: Tanimbar islands (arafura sea)
description: Robust, big-headed, and rather short-tailed parrot endemic to the Tanimbar Islands, where it inhabits lowland and foothill forests. Male bright green with red underwings and orange bill, female bright red with dark underwings and bill.

name: Taveta Golden-Weaver
rangeDescription: Riverine scrub of far southeastern kenya and northeastern tanzania
description: Breeding male is rich yellow with darker orange patches on the breast and the rear part of the crown. The female is dark on the back and buffy yellowish below with a pale base to the bill.

name: Green Avadavat
rangeDescription: Locally in grassland and scrub of peninsular india
description: Very pretty small finch-like bird with red bill, red eyes, and distinctly barred flanks. Sexes are similar, but males have brighter greens and yellows than females.

name: Jambu Fruit-Dove
rangeDescription: Peninsular thailand, malay peninsula, sumatra, borneo and western java
description: The plum-red face and pink “blush” on the white chest of the cartoonish-looking male are unique. Plainer female and juvenile can be difficult to separate from female Black-naped Fruit Dove; look out for Jambu’s bright white eye-ring and orange bill.

name: Tristram's Bunting
rangeDescription: Siberia to northeastern china; winters to southern china and northern thailand
description: Small and distinctive bunting, usually seen moving around quietly in thick undergrowth. Warm rusty brown with a black-and-white striped head.

name: Strange-tailed Tyrant
rangeDescription: Locally in eastern paraguay, southern brazil, uruguay, and northern argentina
description: Striking flycatcher with a spectacular mating display, in which male flies high into the air and repeatedly pumps tails above and then below body. Endemic to the Iberá marshes of NE Argentina and E Paraguay.

name: Chatham Islands Gerygone
rangeDescription: Chatham islands (new zealand)
description: Small warbler endemic to the Chatham Islands of New Zealand. Note dull olive-brown upperparts and white to yellowish plumage below.

name: Small-headed Elaenia
rangeDescription: Southeastern brazil (rio de janeiro) to eastern paraguay and northeastern argentina
description: Medium-sized flycatcher with a small head and long tail. Found in forests and second growth.

name: Laysan Finch
rangeDescription: Laysan island (northwestern hawaiian islands)
description: A finch-billed Hawaiian honeycreeper endemic to the island of Laysan; does not occur in the main Hawaiian Islands. An introduced population occurs on Pearl and Hermes Atoll.

name: Speckled Warbler
rangeDescription: Central and eastern queensland through new south wales to eastern and central victoria
description: Small, distinctive, ground-dwelling bird. Upperparts gray, underparts cream white, with black streaking on back, underparts, and crown.

name: Western Dwarf Hornbill
rangeDescription: Sierra leone to northern democratic republic of the congo (west of the congo river)
description: A small, dark forest hornbill found predominantly in primary forest subcanopy, where it prefers areas with abundant vines. This species is unique in its overall dark coloration and its broad white eyebrow that extends to the back of the head.

name: Wilson's Indigobird
rangeDescription: Senegambia to guinea, eastward to northeastern democratic republic of the congo, south sudan, and western ethiopia
description: A nest parasite that lays its eggs in the nests of Bar-breasted Firefinch. Breeding males are glossy purplish-black with a pale brownish panel in the wings, while females and non-breeding males are brown and streaky on the back and pale below, with a bold facial pattern.

name: Carp's Tit
rangeDescription: Southern angola to northwestern namibia
description: A black tit with a mostly white wing and outer tail. The sexes are similar, but females are slightly duller and browner.

name: Brown-throated Barbet
rangeDescription: Montane forest of western java
description: Unique large barbet of western Java. Leaf-green with a dark bill and an earth-brown head.

name: Saffron Toucanet
rangeDescription: Humid forest of southeastern brazil to northeastern argentina and eastern paraguay
description: Unmistakable yellow toucan with a long two-toned bill: half red and half greenish-yellow. The iris is pale and framed with bare red skin.

name: Fulvous Owl
rangeDescription: Mountains of southern mexico (eastern oaxaca and chiapas) to el salvador
description: The southern counterpart to Barred Owl of the United States, this large brown-eyed owl occurs in highland forests from Oaxaca south to Honduras. Found in pine-oak and evergreen forest where it roosts at all levels, sometimes in fairly open situations.
